mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains persistently below its pre-pandemic median for at least 3 consecutive months, it lowers real discount rates, increasing the present value of expected corporate cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically above the 90th percentile of same-horizon returns during low-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by at least 0.5 percentage points within a month signals labor market strengthening, which tends to boost equity valuations and produce positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 3% AND UNRATE decreases by ≥ 0.5pp in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the correlation between the PAYEMS/UNRATE signal and SPX 20-day forward returns is < 0.2 (Pearson's r).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 2% for two consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL), predicts stronger business demand and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases ≥ 2% for two consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL increases < 0.5% in the same months
failure_condition: Across 50 such windows, the average 5-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months, while manufacturing demand (GDPC1) remains flat or rising, suggests deflationary pressure that reduces discounting of future cash flows and tends to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 ≥ flat in the same months
failure_condition: In 10 such deflationary windows, the 20-day forward return mean is below the 10th percentile of all windows (median negative).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in the monthly RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) above 5% for a single month is interpreted as a liquidity injection that lowers risk premia and produces a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases to > 5% in a single month
failure_condition: Across 20 such episodes, the average 5-day forward return is negative (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in labor turnover (PAYEMS) by at least 10% for three consecutive months indicates reduced labor market friction and increased productivity, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by ≥ 10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 10 such turnover declines, the 60-day forward return mean is below the 5th percentile of all periods (median negative).

mechanism_narrative: When the housing market shows accelerating new home sales (HOUST) month-over-month for two consecutive months while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains above 4%, it signals resilient consumer demand and tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥ 5% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE > 4% in those months
regime_hint: Resilient housing demand with moderate labor market slack
failure_condition: The signal recurs 5 times but is never accompanied by a statistically significant positive 20-day forward return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% combined with a sustained rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) by at least 2% per month is interpreted as a softening inflationary squeeze that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 for 2 consecutive months AND PAYEMS increases ≥ 2% per month in those months
failure_condition: Across 10 such episodes, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically above zero (p > 0.05).
